title: Kähler differentials and the canonical sheaf of a smooth curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves].
The *sheaf of Kähler differentials* of $C$ over $k$ is

$$
\Omega^1_{C/k}:=\Delta^*\bigl(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\bigr)
$$

[def-pc-module-pullback], where $\Delta:C\to C\times_kC$ is the diagonal, a closed immersion
because $C$ is separated over $k$ [def-sc-curves], and
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_{C\times_kC}$ is the ideal sheaf of the
diagonal. By [lem-sc-smooth-proper-diagonal-conormal-differentials] (applied to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$)
this is canonically isomorphic to the sheaf which, on every affine open
$U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq C$, is the
sheaf associated with the $A$-module $\Omega_{A/k}$ of Kähler
differentials of the $k$-algebra $A$ with its universal
derivation $d:A\to\Omega_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].
The *canonical sheaf* of $C$ is

$$
\omega_C:=\Omega^1_{C/k}.
$$
